sourceCoverage.chapterCharacter: Hou Hanshu treatise 26 (百官三): establishment of the Director of the Imperial Clan, Minister of Finance and Privy Treasurer offices with Sima Biao's 本注 and one inserted 漢官 quotation (s0187). Three rulers are named as actors in office history: Emperor Wu (武帝 s0140, 孝武帝 s0180), Emperor Cheng (成帝 s0140, s0145) and Emperor Guangwu (世祖 s0146, s0179, s0180). 中興 (s0011, s0030, s0032, s0061) and 章和 (s0186) are period references, and 王太妃/皇后/貴人 (s0074, s0101) are generic ranks; none is a named individual.
sourceCoverage.readMethod: Every unit's Chinese, literal and idiomatic field read in full in three bounded portions (s0001-s0069 incl. s0187, s0070-s0134, s0135-s0186).
mechanicalChecks: 63 multi-character Chinese numerals checked against both English fields: no mismatch (the s0187 residual is spelled-out English numbers).

Every unit aligned against the Siku Quanshu Wenyuange text of 後漢書 志第二十六 (Kanripo KR2a0009 commit 6db36b6dcbe843b825354c22e9be9193d0137c04, file KR2a0009_036.txt). Differences are glyph variants, the s0027 尋/導 corruption (repaired in English) and received 离官 for 離宮 (s0123, s0180), whose English already reads "detached palaces".
Search of both English fields for each defective term (harsh, Yeeting, Goudu, douse, sealing wax, xun, most senior, chamberlain, beginning with): every occurrence is in the repair batch.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 漢〔官〕曰：「員吏百六十四人，其十八人四科，九人斗食，十六人二百石，文學二十人百石，二十五人佐，七十五人學事，一人官醫。」
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The Han official regulations say: “There were 164 clerks; of these, eighteen were in the four categories, nine received douse-rations, sixteen were at two hundred shi, twenty were literary officials at one hundred shi, twenty-five were assistants, seventy-five were trainees, and one was the official physician.”
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The Han official regulations say: “There were 164 clerks; of these, eighteen were in the four categories, nine were dou-ration (peck-salary) clerks, sixteen were at two hundred shi, twenty were literary officials at one hundred shi, twenty-five were assistants, seventy-five were trainees, and one was the official physician.”
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 斗食 is the lowest Han salary grade, clerks paid by the dou (peck) of grain, listed here between 四科 and the two-hundred-shi grade. "douse-rations" is not an English rendering of 斗食 (斗 dou "peck"); both identical English fields carry the error.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: One director of the chamberlain of the palace seal, six hundred piculs.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: One director of the palace keepers, six hundred piculs.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 守宫令 is literally "director of palace keeping"; the Chinese has no "chamberlain" or "seal". His duties (s0050) are paper, ink, brushes, Secretariat supplies and sealing clay, which the idiomatic field already describes; the literal field invents a title.

sourceWitnesses.excerpt: 主御纸笔墨及尚书财用诸物及封泥

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 本注曰：主御纸笔墨及尚书财用诸物及封泥。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: He supplied the palace with paper, ink, brushes, stationery for the Secretariat, and sealing wax.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: He supplied the palace with paper, ink, brushes, stationery for the Secretariat, and sealing clay.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 封泥 is sealing clay (the literal field already says so); Han documents were sealed with clay, and "sealing wax" is a different, later material.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 法驾出，则多识者一人参乘，余皆骑在乘舆车后。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: On formal processions the most senior gentleman-in-attendance rode in the escort seat beside the emperor; the others followed the carriage on horseback.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: On formal processions the most learned gentleman-in-attendance rode in the escort seat beside the emperor; the others followed the carriage on horseback.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 多識者 is "one of wide knowledge" (the literal field: "one of great knowledge"), not seniority; the commentary on this office stresses learning (蔡質漢儀: 侍中…選舊儒髙徳博學).

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The superintendent of the Goudu palace parks held six hundred piculs.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The superintendent of the Goudun palace parks held six hundred piculs.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 钩盾 is romanized Goudun (盾 dùn); "Goudu" drops the final -n of the office name.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 本注曰：职属少府者，自太医、上林凡四官。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Original note says: As for offices whose duties belong to the Privy Treasurer, from the grand physician and Shanglin, in all four offices.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Original note says: As for offices whose duties belong to the Privy Treasurer, from the grand physician to Shanglin, in all four offices.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 自太医、上林凡四官 is "from the Grand Physician to Shanglin, four offices in all": the chapter lists exactly four Privy Treasurer offices from 太医 (s0037) through 太官 (s0042) and 守宫 (s0049) to 上林 (s0052), after which 侍中 begins the offices attached only by document (s0177 自侍中至御史). The literal "from X and Shanglin" and the idiomatic "beginning with … and Shanglin" misstate Shanglin as a second starting point instead of the end of the range.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 本注曰：职属少府者，自太医、上林凡四官。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Only four bureaus still drew their substantive duties directly from the Privy Treasurer, beginning with the grand physician and Shanglin.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Only four bureaus still drew their substantive duties directly from the Privy Treasurer, from the grand physician through Shanglin.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 自太医、上林凡四官 is "from the Grand Physician to Shanglin, four offices in all": the chapter lists exactly four Privy Treasurer offices from 太医 (s0037) through 太官 (s0042) and 守宫 (s0049) to 上林 (s0052), after which 侍中 begins the offices attached only by document (s0177 自侍中至御史). The literal "from X and Shanglin" and the idiomatic "beginning with … and Shanglin" misstate Shanglin as a second starting point instead of the end of the range.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 章和以下，中官稍广，加尝药、太官、御者、钩盾、尚方、考工、别作监，皆六百石，宦者为之，转为兼副，或省，故录本官。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: After the Zhanghe era the eunuch establishment grew: stewards over tasting, kitchens, equipage, parks, workshops, and separate ateliers at six hundred piculs, often held concurrently or later cut—hence this note preserves their original titles.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: After the Zhanghe era the eunuch establishment grew: stewards over tasting, kitchens, equipage, parks, workshops, the directorate of works, and separate ateliers at six hundred piculs, often held concurrently or later cut—hence this note preserves their original titles.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: The source list 尝药、太官、御者、钩盾、尚方、考工、别作监 has seven overseers; the idiomatic field omits 考工 (the directorate of works, rendered so in s0179), which the literal field includes as "works of artificers".

repairBatchNotes.routing: Worker-authored repairs: route into the active editorial application as a new schema-4 review alongside the retained schema-3 decisions r0001/r0002; a separate reviewer accepts, revises or rejects each. proposalKey values are owner labels; the host assigns native IDs (next free: houhanshu:127:r0003).

deliberatelyNotRepaired.reason: Received 典官婢 (official bondmaids) vs Siku 典宫婢 (palace bondmaids): either reading fits and the English (literal "official slave girls", idiomatic "palace bondmaids/women") is defensible under both.
Received 漢〔官〕曰 is an editorial emendation (Siku commentary reads 漢書曰); "The Han official regulations say" follows the received emendation and is kept.
成帝初署 can be read "early in Emperor Cheng's reign appointed" (literal) or "Emperor Cheng first appointed" (idiomatic); both are defensible and neither changes the reign-bounded chronology.

distinctHolds.classification: representation question about source-supported reign containers; not a concrete source contradiction, attribution error or missing date
evidence: The Chinese attributes each act to the named ruler (s0140 武帝用宦者…成帝用士人; s0145 成帝初署尚書四人; s0146 世祖承遵…凡六曹; s0179 世祖改屬司農…; s0180 孝武帝初置水衡都尉…世祖省之), so each act falls within that ruler's reign. The chapter gives no year or era for any of them, so no narrower in-chapter date exists.
Reign spans agree with the canonical dossiers found by bounded lookup: Liu Che BC 141-87, Liu Ao BC 33-7, Liu Xiu AD 25-57.
Every row already uses certainty explicit-event-contextual-date with the reign label as sourceDate, i.e. the interval is the dating context of the act, not a claimed duration.

Precedent in the same treatise series under the same audit contract: houhanshu/122 claim-348 (sourceDate 武帝置, BC 141-87) and houhanshu/126 claim-1 (世祖中興, AD 25-57) and claim-49 (武帝, BC 141-87) were independently approved as conservative reign-era containers, 126 on 2026-09-29 after this hold.
